title: Ending a NSW tenancy
description: Steps for ending a NSW tenancy on a ground and closing out the bond. Summarised from NSW Fair Trading pages.

sources.title: Minimum notice periods for ending a residential tenancy
Rental Bonds Online for self-managing landlords

items.title: Identify the ground for ending the tenancy
items.detail: Since 19 May 2025 there is no ending a tenancy without a reason, even at the end of a fixed term.

items.title: Check the notice period for that ground and agreement type
items.detail: For example 90 days for a proposed sale on a periodic agreement, 30 days after a sale contract requiring vacant possession, 14 days for breach or unpaid rent.

items.title: Attach the supporting documents the ground needs
items.detail: For example the proposed contract or agency agreement for a proposed sale, or a signed and dated statement for renovations or moving in.

items.title: Allow 7 extra working days if you post the notice
Complete the final condition report with the tenant and take photos
Claim the bond through Rental Bonds Online, or the Claim for Refund of Bond Money form for a paper bond
If the tenant doesn't agree, give them the condition report and quotes or invoices within 7 days of claiming
Get all keys back and note the water meter reading
